reused_fixtures.role: The fixture every non-failure section of OnDiscMSExperiment_test.cpp opens: 2 spectra, 1 chromatogram, instrument 'LTQ FT' with 1 mass analyzer. Committed by tests/data/indexed_mzml_provenance.json.
The indexed fixture of the precursor-m/z filter section: 4 spectra, index 1 is MS2 with precursor m/z 5.55. Committed by tests/data/mzml_schema_provenance.json.

The fixture every failure section of OnDiscMSExperiment_test.cpp opens: plain mzML with no indexListOffset footer, so openFile returns false while loadMetaData_ still runs. It declares 4 spectra and 2 chromatograms, which is what distinguishes 'no records in the index' from 'no records at all'. Committed by tests/data/mzml_schema_provenance.json.

derived_fixtures.written_to: a temporary directory at test time; nothing is committed
derived_fixtures.derivation: The second spectrum's native identifier 'controllerType=0 controllerNumber=1 scan=2' is rewritten to '...scan=1' at both of its two occurrences: the <spectrum> element's id attribute and the idRef of its <indexList> offset. The two identifiers are the same length, so every byte offset in the index stays correct; the test asserts the occurrence count and the preserved file length before using the file.
derived_fixtures.reason: No START_SECTION of OnDiscMSExperiment_test.cpp uses a duplicate native identifier, and the upstream fixture's identifiers are unique, so the documented first-wins rule has no upstream input to assert it with.

source_anchors.operation: @note: unlike in-memory loading, a spectrum failing the RT or MS-level filter is returned with metadata and no peaks, so every index still maps to the file
@note: not thread-safe because one file pointer is moved per access; the class documentation recommends #pragma omp parallel for firstprivate(ondisc_map)
copy constructor copies filename_, indexed_mzml_file_ (whose own copy reopens the stream and loses its native-id maps), meta_ms_experiment_ and options_, but not the facade's own two native-id caches
operator== falls back to comparing the two meta_ms_experiment_ pointers when either is null, so a skipMetaData experiment never equals one that loaded its metadata
isSortedByRT returns false without metadata and otherwise meta_ms_experiment_->isSorted(false), i.e. RT order only
size() is getNrSpectra() and empty() is getNrSpectra() == 0; chromatograms never affect either
getExperimentalSettings static_pointer_casts meta_ms_experiment_, so it returns a null pointer after openFile(..., true); the header documents no such case
getMetaData hands out a mutable shared_ptr<PeakMap> to the metadata the facade is using
getSpectrumById and getChromatogramById return OpenMS::Interfaces pointers straight from the handler, bypassing both the metadata and options_
assignment operator is declared private and never defined, because the handler's file streams cannot be copied
typedef OpenMS::OnDiscMSExperiment OnDiscPeakMap
openFile assigns filename_ first, then opens the index, then loads the metadata, and returns the handler's parsing success; a throwing metadata load leaves the object naming the new file
an empty filename or skipMetaData skips loadMetaData_ entirely
setSkipXMLChecks forwards to the handler only; it is never written into options_, and openFile does not reset it
loadMetaData_ always loads ALL metadata unfiltered with setFillData(false), to keep index correspondence with the handler
getMetaChromatogramById_ rebuilds chromatograms_native_ids_ only when it is empty, and openFile never clears it
Exception::IllegalArgument "Could not find chromatogram with id '<id>'." for an identifier the metadata does not carry
getChromatogramByNativeId and getSpectrumByNativeId (line 116) consult no option at all; with metadata they merge the handler's peaks into the metadata record
getSpectrum: RT range checked against DRange::encloses before any peak I/O, returning the metadata-only spectrum
MS-level filter checked before peak I/O, with the UInt level narrowed to Int by containsMSLevel
precursor m/z filter uses only getPrecursors()[0] and is skipped entirely for a spectrum with no precursor
getMSSpectrumById(int, MSSpectrum&) merges the decoded peak arrays into the metadata spectrum, preserving its other fields
without metadata the full spectrum is loaded and the RT, MS-level and precursor filters are silently not applied
the m/z and intensity filter path assigns only the SpectrumSettings base into a fresh MSSpectrum, so retention time, MS level, drift time, name and the float/integer/string data arrays are lost
getChromatogram applies no before-I/O filter: the record is always read, and the RT range then selects points rather than dropping the chromatogram
the chromatogram filter path assigns only the ChromatogramSettings base, so name and the three data arrays are lost
encloses(position) returns false for position < min and for position >= max, i.e. the interval is half-open
retention_time_, drift_time_, drift_time_unit_, ms_level_, name_ and the three data arrays are MSSpectrum members, not SpectrumSettings members
name_ and the three data arrays are MSChromatogram members, not ChromatogramSettings members
domParseSpectrum(const std::string&, MSSpectrum&) appends the decoded peaks and auxiliary arrays to the caller's spectrum and overwrites only its native id
store dereferences exp.getExperimentalSettings() with no null check, so storing an experiment opened with skipMetaData dereferences a null shared_ptr
store walks getNrSpectra() through getSpectrum and getNrChromatograms() through getChromatogram; this loop is the materialisation load_experiment reproduces
the OnDiscMSExperiment(const std::string&) section is commented out because no such constructor exists; its assertion is tmp.size() == 2
TEST_REAL_SIMILAR(precursor_mz, 5.55) for spectrum index 1 of MzMLFile_4_indexed.mzML

evidence: Tier 3 (source review). Every expected value in tests/on_disc_experiment.rs is a literal transcribed from OnDiscMSExperiment_test.cpp and its unmodified fixtures - 2 spectra, 1 chromatogram, 19914 and 19800 peaks, 48 chromatogram points, instrument 'LTQ FT' with 1 mass analyzer, native ids 'controllerType=0 controllerNumber=1 scan=1' and '...scan=2' and 'TIC', m/z window 400-600, intensity window 1000-1000000, and from MzMLFile_4_indexed.mzML the MS2 at index 1 with precursor m/z 5.55 - or a value read from the same fixture through this crate's own metadata load (scan start times 0.2961 s and 0.4738 s, peak counts 15 and 10), or - for the failure sections, which open the unmodified non-indexed MzMLFile_1.mzML - the 4 spectra and 2 chromatograms that file's spectrumList and chromatogramList declare. No C++ was built or executed and no retained C++ output was used, so nothing here is tier 1 or tier 2. Tier 4 (independently derived) covers what the source does not check or does not have: the resource ceilings, the atomicity of a failed open_file, the half-open DRange endpoints exercised at a spectrum's own RT, load_experiment, try_clone resolving native identifiers where a source copy cannot, and the documented fact that the by-native-id fetches ignore the options. Class-test section accounting: 29 START_SECTION occurrences, of which 28 are live and 1 (line 53) is commented out upstream; 29 ported, 0 mapped-with-evidence, 0 unaccounted. The two Interfaces pointer sections are ported onto the single peak vector that replaces their two arrays, because the crate has no OpenSWATH Interfaces layer.
gaps: No tier 1 differential: reaching it would need an oracle driver over OnDiscMSExperiment in ../oracle/drivers/, printing full-precision peak arrays and the filtered variants for each record of IndexedmzMLFile_1.mzML. Not built here.

The documented first-wins rule for duplicate native identifiers is only observable at the index layer. mzML requires unique record identifiers and this crate's reader enforces it, so a metadata load carrying a duplicate is refused before the facade's identifier_caches runs; its or_insert_with is defensive. a_duplicate_native_identifier_resolves_to_the_first_record asserts the refusal and, via skip_metadata, the index layer's first-wins. Reaching the facade cache's own branch would need a way to install metadata without the reader, which the public API does not offer.

This manifest is not listed in SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json, so tools/check_core_sdk.py does not verify the hashes recorded here. The MzMLFile_1.mzML hash was checked by hand against the pinned copy and against the second in-tree copy at tests/data/mzml_header/MzMLFile_1.original.mzML. Registering the manifest is the integrator's step.

The source parallelises nothing in this class, but its own class documentation recommends copying it per OpenMP thread. This port is serial; every fetch takes &mut self and a second reader is a second open or try_clone. The performance gap is stated, not closed.

setSkipXMLChecks is ported: it maps to the handler's options_mut().skip_xml_checks, which reaches the Base64 whitespace strip at src/format/mzml.rs:2386. The fixture's arrays carry no whitespace, so the test can assert that the flag is carried and the decode still succeeds, not that a whitespace-bearing array decodes differently.

The Interfaces::Spectrum / Interfaces::Chromatogram pointer overloads are not ported; the crate has no OpenSWATH Interfaces layer (INTERFACES/DataStructures.h is unmapped in docs/core-sdk-coverage.json).
IndexedMzMLFileLoader itself is not ported; only the materialisation loop of its store is, as load_experiment.
